title: Firebase Analytics: start collection only after consent
steps: Use the manifest flag, not a runtime call in Application.onCreate — a runtime call races the automatic first_open event.
Persist the user's choice and re-apply it on every launch.

title: Firebase Crashlytics: opt-in crash reporting
steps: If you rely on a legitimate use for crash reporting, document it in your notice.

title: Meta (Facebook) SDK: delay initialisation and app events
code:
// After the user taps Accept:
FacebookSdk.setAutoInitEnabled(true)
FacebookSdk.fullyInitialize()
FacebookSdk.setAutoLogAppEventsEnabled(true)
FacebookSdk.setAdvertiserIDCollectionEnabled(true)
steps: If you call AppEventsLogger.activateApp(), make sure the SDK is initialised first — with auto-init off it is not.

title: Google Mobile Ads: gather consent before initialising ads
steps: Do not call MobileAds.initialize() or load ads before the user's choice.
For child-facing apps, do not serve targeted ads at all (DPDP s.9(3)).

title: AppsFlyer: init, but start only after consent
steps: Do not call start() before consent; use stop(true, context) if consent is withdrawn.

title: Adjust: initialise only after consent
code:
// After the user taps Accept (Adjust SDK v5):
Adjust.initSdk(adjustConfig)
steps: Move SDK initialisation out of Application.onCreate into your consent callback.
Check your SDK version's method names in the vendor docs.

title: Branch: keep tracking disabled until consent
steps: Confirm the exact API for your Branch SDK version.

title: CleverTap: opt out until consent
steps: Confirm the opt-out API for your CleverTap SDK version.

title: Mixpanel: opt out of tracking by default
Amplitude: start opted out
code:
// Create Amplitude with optOut = true in its configuration, then after consent:
amplitude.configuration.optOut = false
steps: Confirm the configuration field for your Amplitude SDK version.

title: Add a DPDP notice and consent screen on first launch
steps: Show the notice before initialising any non-essential SDK.
List the personal data, the specific purposes, how to withdraw, and how to complain to the Data Protection Board.
Record the user's choice with a timestamp (you must be able to prove it — s.6(10)).

title: Default every optional consent toggle to OFF
code: Checkbox(checked = analyticsConsent, onCheckedChange = { analyticsConsent = it }) // initial value: false
steps: Only the user's own tap may switch a consent option on (clear affirmative action, s.6(1)).

title: Make 'Reject' as easy as 'Accept'
steps: Put a 'Reject' button on the first screen, with the same size and visual weight as 'Accept'.
Do not hide refusal behind 'Manage' or extra screens.
Withdrawal later must be equally easy (s.6(4)).

title: Ask for each purpose separately
steps: Split into separate choices, e.g. Essential (explained, no toggle), Analytics, Personalised offers.
Store and honour each choice independently.

title: Itemise the data and state the purpose
steps: List each personal data item (e.g. phone number, device ID, purchase history).
State the specific purpose and the service it enables (Rule 3(b)).

title: Show how to withdraw consent, use rights and complain
steps: Add 'You can withdraw consent anytime in Settings › Privacy' with a direct link.
Explain how to exercise rights and how to complain to the Data Protection Board (Rule 3(c)).

title: Offer the notice in Indian languages
steps: Add a language picker for the notice: English plus Hindi and your users' regional languages (Eighth Schedule, s.5(3)).

title: Child-facing app: no tracking, verifiable parental consent
steps: Remove or disable ad and behavioural-tracking SDKs for children (s.9(3)).
Obtain verifiable consent from a parent before processing a child's data (s.9(1)).
